samples.evidence: Individual semistructured interviews were conducted with 12 relatives of male farmers who had died by suicide in Queensland or New South Wales, Australia (2006-2014). Twelve male farmers (including 1 farm manager) (Mage = 60.17, SD = 7.17), who died by suicide, were each represented by an informant, a close next-of kin (NOK) who had lived with or known the deceased well. Semistructured telephone interviews were conducted in a confidential room with 12 individuals who had lost a close NOK male farmer to suicide. Twelve participants were included in the analysis. Table 1 Characteristics of the Australian Male Farmers Who Died by Suicide and Interviewed NOK. The present study extends understanding of suicide among Australian male farmers using a qualitative approach to analyze PA interviews with close relatives.
